6bbde2a5d2efdb3e.heading: Interest and alternative finance payments eligible for relief on qualifying loans and alternative finance arrangements (Self Assessment helpsheet HS340)

amounts.name: Limit on Income Tax reliefs
amounts.value: greater of £50,000 and 25% of 'adjusted total income'

caveats: For tax year 6 April 2025 to 5 April 2026, relief cannot be claimed for the cost of getting a loan/alternative finance, or interest on it, where funds are used for residential property in a partnership's property business — this is instead used to calculate a reduction in Income Tax in box 12.
Relief does not apply to overdraft or credit card interest.
Equipment/machinery loan interest relief only applies if capital allowances could be claimed on the item(s), and only the business-use proportion qualifies if used partly for other purposes.
MTD for Income Tax users must use compatible software rather than the SA return boxes referenced in this helpsheet.

definitions.meaning: Someone who works for the greater part of their time as a director or employee of the company or of a subsidiary in which the company has an interest of 51% or more

A loan or alternative finance arrangement where borrowed money is used for specified purposes (e.g. buying shares in a close company, acquiring partnership interest, buying business equipment) entitling the borrower to interest/payment relief

obligations.must: obtain and keep a certificate of interest or alternative finance payments from the lender
obligations.trigger: claiming relief for interest/alternative finance payments
obligations.who: Self Assessment taxpayer claiming qualifying loan interest relief

obligations.must: make claims and adjustments through compatible software instead of SA return boxes
obligations.trigger: mandated use of MTD for Income Tax
obligations.who: Taxpayer using Making Tax Digital for Income Tax

note.summary: HS340 explains how to claim relief for interest on qualifying loans and alternative finance payments in box 5 of the 'other tax reliefs' section (page Ai 2) of the SA101 additional information pages. It lists qualifying purposes (close company shares/loans, employee-controlled companies, co-operatives, partnership interests, equipment/machinery), excludes overdraft/credit card interest, and covers the residential property finance costs restriction, the overall limit on Income Tax reliefs, record-keeping requirements, and beneficial loan interest benefits. It also notes that Making Tax Digital for Income Tax users will make claims via compatible software instead of these SA boxes.
